paragraphs: ACTG-ARL addresses a practical tension in private synthetic text: the output should protect users while retaining useful statistical properties and following detailed generation instructions. The paper separates this problem into learning features and generating text conditioned on those features. This gives the generator an explicit description of what the synthetic text should preserve.

Through ablation experiments, the authors identify a configuration combining a rich tabular feature schema, a differentially private tabular synthesizer, and a conditional text generator fine-tuned with differential privacy. They call this combination ACTG. The hierarchy makes attribute preservation an explicit part of the generation process rather than leaving it entirely to end-to-end text synthesis.

The second contribution, Anchored RL, improves conditional instruction following after training. It combines reinforcement learning with supervised fine-tuning on best-of-N data, using the supervised component as an anchor against reward hacking. Together, the components improve control and deliver a reported 20% MAUVE improvement over prior work while retaining strong privacy guarantees.
icml-2026-actg-arl-differentially-privat.tldr: ACTG-ARL combines private attribute modeling, conditional generation, and anchored reinforcement learning to improve synthetic text quality and control.

paragraphs: Reusing trained models, either directly or through fine-tuning, makes it useful to measure how closely two models are related. The paper studies this as model cloning, motivated by model lineage, intellectual property, and information security. It introduces a definition of model cloning and a detection framework designed for trained neural networks.

The framework examines two complementary aspects of a model. At the structural level, it represents computation through normalized graphs, allowing model topology to be compared. At the weight level, it measures statistical similarity between learned parameters without requiring explicit parameter alignment. Together, these views account for both how a model computes and the numerical values it has learned.

Experiments on a synthetic clone benchmark and real-world open-source models show that the method can accurately identify similar models. The contribution is a unified, extensible quantitative basis for comparing models beyond existing code-clone detection techniques. This supports applications such as finding related models, studying their lineage, and informing model intellectual property protection.
icml-2026-an-in-depth-study-on-deep-lear.tldr: The paper detects model similarity by combining normalized computational graphs with weight statistics that do not require explicit parameter alignment.

paragraphs: RNA inverse design starts with a desired secondary structure and seeks a sequence that will fold into it. CocoRNA tackles the difficulty of this search by dividing the design problem into smaller subproblems. Multiple reinforcement learning agents collaborate on these subproblems, reducing complexity and improving exploration of possible design strategies.

Coordination comes from a centralized critic during training. This critic has access to global structural information and uses it to guide the agents toward jointly useful decisions. The approach therefore combines smaller design responsibilities with feedback about the overall structure. That connection matters because solving individual parts should contribute to a successful complete RNA design.

On the Rfam dataset, CocoRNA substantially improves both success rate and design speed over state-of-the-art methods. Its learned policies also generalize to unseen structures without further training. Additional experiments on other biological sequence design tasks support the framework’s broader potential, extending the evidence beyond RNA structure design while keeping the central contribution a cooperative learning approach.
icml-2026-cocorna-collective-rna-design-.tldr: CocoRNA trains cooperating agents to design RNA sequences, improving reported success and speed while generalizing to unseen structures.

paragraphs: DART studies targeted adversarial examples created using open-source multimodal language models and transferred to closed-source models. A central problem is overfitting: making an adversarial example closely resemble one target example in a source model’s hidden representation may not produce an attack that transfers well. The paper replaces this single-example alignment with a distributional view.

DART treats augmented versions of an image as samples from an underlying distribution associated with that image. It then uses Energy Distance, a non-parametric measure of distribution difference, to align these distributions in hidden representation space. This aims to capture image semantics more generally than matching particular representations alone.

A second component learns relationships between source and target models using a graph neural network. Those relationships guide adaptive selection of surrogate models for different targets. Benchmark experiments report better robustness and effectiveness than competing approaches. The results support combining broader semantic alignment with target-sensitive surrogate selection when studying how adversarial examples transfer between multimodal models.
icml-2026-dart-distribution-aware-adapti.tldr: DART improves adversarial transfer through distribution-level image alignment and learned selection of surrogate multimodal models.

paragraphs: ECHO addresses speculative decoding when many language-model requests run concurrently. In this setting, checking speculative candidates can become the main computational bottleneck. The paper argues that fixed candidate trees waste verification work, while dynamically constructed trees can accumulate poor decisions and encounter incompatibilities with computational kernels.

Integrated into SGLang, ECHO treats speculative execution as a scheduling problem with a limited budget. It combines the batch into a unified candidate tree and uses sparse confidence gating to allocate that budget. Allocation can shift between deeper speculation and wider branching, balancing fewer overall verification steps against the efficiency of each step.

Evaluations cover different model scales, including Qwen3-235B, and both low-load and high-load serving conditions. ECHO consistently outperforms the evaluated state-of-the-art baselines, with up to 5.35-fold walltime speedup and more than 20% relative speedup gain against the strongest baselines. These findings support allocating speculation jointly across a batch when verification cost constrains serving throughput, rather than evaluating speculative choices only in isolation.
icml-2026-echo-elastic-speculative-decod.tldr: ECHO dynamically budgets speculative decoding across a batch to reduce verification waste and improve serving speed under concurrent workloads.

paragraphs: Knowledge-based visual question answering requires connecting an image and question to relevant external knowledge. Fine-grained entity identification makes this difficult: visual ambiguity can send retrieval toward the wrong knowledge, particularly when image and text signals are handled separately. EntRAG organizes retrieval around entities to make this connection more explicit.

Its EntBind component binds entity tokens to latent visual features and aligns the query with multimodal entity representations. This produces candidate entities that reflect both visual information and the question. A reranker then selects useful context by considering entity-level alignment alongside relevance to the overall query. The selected evidence feeds a context-aware answer generator.

The approach matters because identifying the right entity and choosing useful evidence are treated as connected steps before answer generation. Experiments report consistently stronger results than prior methods, including scores of 46.1 on E-VQA and 44.5 on InfoSeek. These findings support entity-centered retrieval as a way to obtain more consistent and reliable answers when precise visual grounding is required.
icml-2026-entrag-entity-centric-retrieva.tldr: EntRAG connects visual features to entities, reranks their evidence, and uses the selected context to improve knowledge-based visual question answering.

paragraphs: EvoMAS automates the design of systems containing multiple language-model agents. The paper identifies a tradeoff in existing approaches: generated code can fail to execute reliably, while rigid architectural templates restrict the systems that can be expressed. EvoMAS instead searches over structured configurations describing candidate multi-agent systems.

The search follows an evolutionary process. It selects configurations from a pool, mutates them using feedback, and combines configurations through crossover. Execution traces guide these changes, while an experience memory and the candidate pool are repeatedly refined. This makes observed system behavior part of the process for deciding which designs to explore next.

Across reasoning, software engineering, and tool-use benchmarks, EvoMAS improves task performance, executability, and runtime robustness over evaluated alternatives. It exceeds EvoAgent by 10.5 points on BBEH and 7.1 points on WorkBench. With Claude-4.5-Sonnet, it reaches 79.1% on SWE-Bench-Verified, which the paper reports as matching the leaderboard’s top performance. These results support configuration evolution as a practical approach to automated multi-agent design.
icml-2026-evomas-evolutionary-generation.tldr: EvoMAS evolves structured multi-agent configurations using execution feedback, improving reported task performance and runtime reliability.

paragraphs: FedReLa addresses federated learning when class imbalance and differences between clients occur together. A class may be rare across the full system yet have a different frequency locally, and some clients may lack it entirely. These mismatches can bias the combined model, while the unknown global class distribution makes data-level correction difficult.

The method uses a feature-dependent label re-allocator to relabel samples and correct biased global decision boundaries. Its distinguishing property is that it does not need the overall class distribution. By acting at the data level, FedReLa provides a modular intervention that can be combined with algorithmic methods rather than depending on a particular model architecture.

Experiments on stepwise-imbalanced and long-tailed datasets show significant improvements in both minority-class accuracy and overall accuracy, exceeding the previous state of the art. The paper also reports consistent gains when integrating the method with algorithmic approaches, without extra communication overhead. This makes relabeling a complementary tool for handling imbalance and client heterogeneity within decentralized training.
icml-2026-fedrela-imbalanced-federated-l.tldr: FedReLa uses feature-dependent relabeling to improve imbalanced federated learning without knowing global class frequencies or adding communication overhead.

paragraphs: Multi-objective reinforcement learning produces behaviors that trade off competing goals. Presenting a person with many possible policies can make selection difficult, but asking them to specify exact preferences beforehand is also unrealistic. This paper brings the decision maker into optimization so preferred behaviors can be discovered through interaction.

The framework learns implicit preferences in real time without requiring prior knowledge of them. It integrates that learning directly into parallel policy optimization, balancing exploration of possibilities with refinement of promising options. Human feedback therefore helps shape the search itself, connecting policy improvement to what the decision maker actually wants.

In a quadrupedal robot simulation, interactions enable the method to find policies aligned with human preferences, including running like a dog. Further experiments cover seven MuJoCo tasks and a multi-microgrid design problem, with comparisons against eight state-of-the-art algorithms supporting the framework’s effectiveness. The findings show how interactive preference discovery can help identify useful policies while optimization is still underway, reducing reliance on fully specified preferences at the outset.
icml-2026-human-in-the-loop-policy-optim.tldr: The framework learns human preferences during policy optimization to discover behaviors that balance multiple objectives in personally useful ways.

paragraphs: Interactive segmentation uses user clicks to improve an image’s predicted object mask. After a global prediction, local refinement focuses on a region near the latest click. Choosing that region matters: a fixed window ignores how the click relates to object geometry, while a separate estimation stage adds computational cost.

EFPNet uses a one-stage framework to predict an error mask from previous feedback and the new click. It derives a focused refinement region from the mask’s largest connected component. Correction then considers relationships in the image, its features, and the predicted mask. A clicked-with-focus mechanism further supports efficient integration of user feedback.

The central contribution is to make the refinement region responsive to the current segmentation error and interaction history. This connects where the system looks next with the correction the user is requesting. Studies on four benchmarks report strong performance in both segmentation effectiveness and computational overhead, supporting the value of learning a more precise focus region within an integrated refinement framework.
icml-2026-interactive-segmentation-with-.tldr: EFPNet predicts where segmentation needs correction and uses that learned focus region to integrate user clicks efficiently.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to identify the best option while satisfying several performance constraints. Each option, or arm, is evaluated across metrics and covariates, with mean performance assumed to depend linearly on arm and covariate features. The goal is to maximize one metric while keeping the others below specified thresholds for every covariate, at a fixed confidence level.

The authors first derive an instance-dependent lower bound on how many samples this task requires. Its multi-level optimization accounts for both whether an arm is feasible and whether it is best. They then design an algorithm that asymptotically matches the bound, establishing that the bound is tight.

Because that algorithm is computationally demanding, the paper develops a relaxed bound through a surrogate problem and its convex dual. The resulting decomposition algorithm updates only two coordinates and takes one gradient step per iteration. It theoretically achieves the relaxed bound and performs effectively in numerical experiments, providing a computationally efficient counterpart to the original sample-optimal construction.
icml-2026-learning-the-best-under-constr.tldr: The paper derives sample-complexity limits for constrained best-arm identification and uses convex duality to build an efficient relaxed algorithm.

paragraphs: MoLF predicts spatial gene expression from histology across multiple cancer types. The paper argues that separate models for individual tissues miss biological patterns shared across cancers and are difficult to apply where data are scarce. Training across cancers can exploit shared information, but the resulting tissue diversity challenges a single undifferentiated architecture.

The proposed model combines conditional flow matching with a mixture of experts. Flow matching learns a transformation from noise into a latent representation of gene expression. Specialized subnetworks parameterize that transformation, with inputs dynamically routed among them. This separates the optimization of different tissue patterns while retaining a shared framework for pan-cancer prediction.

On pan-cancer benchmarks, MoLF consistently outperforms both specialized models and foundation-model baselines, establishing the reported state of the art. It also shows zero-shot generalization to cross-species data. The authors interpret that result as suggesting the model captures conserved relationships between tissue appearance and molecular activity; the cross-species finding supports that possibility rather than establishing the biological mechanism directly.
icml-2026-molf-mixture-of-latent-flow-fo.tldr: MoLF combines flow matching and specialized experts to improve pan-cancer gene-expression prediction from histology, with reported cross-species generalization.

paragraphs: This paper studies finite-horizon multi-objective reinforcement learning in linear Markov decision processes under two information protocols. In one, potentially adversarial preference weights are revealed before each episode. In the other, exploration observes transitions without rewards or preferences, and the collected information must later support arbitrary preference queries.

The analysis identifies why standard shortcuts can break guarantees. Applying future weights to past stochastic rewards disrupts the probabilistic structure used for confidence bounds. The proposed reward interface instead estimates each reward coordinate separately and combines them only when answering a query. The paper also formalizes evaluation when policies may be randomized at episode start, accounting for the resulting convex combinations of returns.

The results give protocol-safe regret bounds with only logarithmic dependence on the number of objectives and near-minimax rates under the stated linear setting. For preference-free exploration, the theory separates learning enough to answer decision queries from explicitly recovering the transition model. This distinction clarifies how the information required for good decisions can differ from the information required for full model reconstruction.
icml-2026-near-minimax-multi-objective-r.tldr: The paper develops near-minimax multi-objective learning guarantees that respect when preferences and rewards become available.

paragraphs: This paper asks what happens inside a language model when context repeatedly asserts the same claim. Looking only at whether the final answer changes can hide the process producing that outcome. The authors introduce a theoretical framework that characterizes contextual influence through the model’s internal inference dynamics, allowing more quantitative analysis.

The analysis finds that repeated assertions do not cause predictive representations to drift without bound. Instead, those representations approach stable regimes that depend on the query. These regimes constrain whether context can change the prediction. Repetition therefore does not function as indefinitely accumulating evidence: for some cases, even unbounded repetition may fail to change the answer, while in others a change becomes inevitable.

Experiments across diverse models and tasks closely match the theoretical predictions. The findings give repetition-based prompting a more precise interpretation: its effect depends on the query-specific inference regime, rather than simply on how often a statement appears. This provides a basis for designing and evaluating prompts that rely on repeated contextual influence.
icml-2026-not-all-answers-are-contextual.tldr: Repeated contextual assertions drive predictions toward query-dependent stable regimes, so repetition may either fail to change an answer or make change inevitable.

paragraphs: Structured state-space duality describes how the same sequence transformation can be implemented as either a recurrent state-space model or a particular masked attention mechanism. The established scalar-identity case offers a linear-time recurrence and a quadratic-time attention realization. This paper formalizes that relationship and investigates how far it extends.

The authors generalize the duality to state-space models with diagonal state matrices. These models support richer dynamics while matching the scalar case’s training-complexity lower bounds. The paper also establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for a state-space model to be equivalent to attention with the specified 1-semiseparable causal mask, making the boundary of that equivalence explicit.

The analysis additionally shows that the duality does not extend to standard softmax attention because of rank explosion. This is a concrete boundary on the connection between these model families. Together, the results broaden the class of state-space dynamics covered by the theory while clarifying which attention structures permit an equivalent recurrent realization.
icml-2026-on-structured-state-space-dual.tldr: The paper extends state-space–attention duality to diagonal dynamics and precisely characterizes its applicability and failure for standard softmax attention.

paragraphs: OSCS addresses a gap between detecting malicious language-model inputs and explicitly controlling how often such inputs are accepted. A defense can perform well empirically without providing control at a user-chosen false acceptance rate. The paper focuses on the practical setting where inputs arrive as a stream and malicious calibration examples are unavailable.

The framework builds on detection scores from existing defenses. It uses recursive density estimation on the test stream to estimate benign probabilities, then makes accept-or-reject decisions in real time. This adds an online selection mechanism to existing detection signals, connecting the decision process to a specified false acceptance target.

Under mild assumptions, the theory bounds the false acceptance rate by the target plus an excess term that vanishes. The qualification matters: the guarantee is expressed through that bound rather than exact finite-stream equality to the target. Experiments involving backdoor and jailbreak attacks show robust false acceptance control across diverse settings and stronger performance than the evaluated baselines.
icml-2026-oscs-online-selection-with-pro.tldr: OSCS uses streaming detection scores to control false acceptance up to a vanishing excess term under mild assumptions, without malicious calibration data.

paragraphs: Parameter Manifold Purification approaches degraded model performance as a problem of corrupted parameters. Motivated by image denoising, it aims to recover cleaner parameters rather than relying on a separate costly optimization procedure for each scenario or architecture. The paper considers degradation associated with imbalanced samples, inaccurate labels, and backdoor attacks.

The method first organizes the large, structured parameter space into nested local clusters viewed as manifolds. An implicit manifold autoencoder then learns compact representations of those clusters. A parameter-cluster discrepancy loss supports removing redundancy while preserving global parameter information. An implicit conditional diffusion model denoises the compact representations to progressively restore clean parameters.

Experiments across three representative degradation scenarios report accurate and complete purification of corrupted parameters in unseen models, together with rapid performance improvements. The significance is the proposed transfer of a denoising-style approach to model parameters themselves. Within the reported experiments, a learned purification procedure can operate on previously unseen models, extending the idea beyond repairing only models encountered during training.
icml-2026-parameter-manifold-purificatio.tldr: Parameter Manifold Purification compresses and denoises parameter clusters to restore degraded models, including unseen models in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Sycophancy occurs when a reasoning model follows a user’s incorrect beliefs or misinformation instead of maintaining independent reasoning. The paper argues that judging and correcting only completed answers misses how this behavior develops along the reasoning trajectory. MONICA moves monitoring and intervention into the generation process itself.

The framework combines a monitor with a calibrator. As the model generates reasoning steps, the monitor assigns scores describing sycophantic drift. When those scores exceed predefined thresholds, the calibrator dynamically suppresses the behavior. The intervention therefore does not require waiting for a complete answer, allowing the framework to respond to problematic drift during intermediate reasoning.

Experiments across 12 datasets and three large reasoning models show reductions in sycophancy in both intermediate steps and final answers, alongside robust performance improvements. The contribution is the coupling of step-level observation with immediate calibration. These findings support treating sycophancy as behavior that can emerge during a response and be addressed before generation finishes, rather than evaluating only its final expression.
icml-2026-real-time-monitoring-and-calib.tldr: MONICA monitors sycophantic drift during reasoning and triggers calibration before the model finishes its answer.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models can decode multiple tokens in parallel, but block-wise systems often retain only confident token predictions and discard the rest through remasking. This paper shows that discarded representations still contain useful context. Residual Context Diffusion, or RCD, aims to preserve that information for later decoding iterations.

RCD converts discarded token representations into contextual residuals and injects them into the next denoising step. A decoupled two-stage training pipeline avoids the backpropagation-related memory bottlenecks associated with the method. The authors demonstrate conversion of a standard diffusion language model using approximately 300 million tokens, evaluating both long-chain reasoning with SDAR and short-chain instruction following with LLaDA.

Across a broad set of benchmarks, RCD improves accuracy by 4–11 percentage points with minimal additional computation. On the most challenging AIME tasks, it nearly doubles baseline accuracy and requires up to four to five times fewer denoising steps at the baseline’s peak accuracy. The results show that information from discarded predictions can improve both answer quality and decoding efficiency.
icml-2026-residual-context-diffusion-lan.tldr: RCD recycles discarded diffusion-token representations as context, improving reported accuracy and reducing denoising steps needed to match baseline performance.

paragraphs: Vision-language models enable detection of unfamiliar classes without access to in-distribution training data. Existing methods often use text representations of class names as reference points for deciding whether an image belongs to a known class. This paper questions that choice by analyzing the mismatch between textual reference points and optimal visual ones.

The theory shows that these off-the-shelf textual prototypes are generally misaligned with optimal prototypes in visual feature space. Prompt engineering alone cannot eliminate this intrinsic modality gap. The proposed framework instead learns visual class prototypes online, using unlabeled test-time inputs and the pretrained model’s soft predictions as pseudo-supervision.

The authors provide convergence guarantees for the online optimization and report state-of-the-art results across several out-of-distribution detection settings. The method matters because it adapts the reference points in the feature space where images are represented, while retaining the post-hoc setting without in-distribution training data. The findings connect a theoretical weakness in text-based prototypes to a practical online correction.
icml-2026-respecting-modality-gap-in-pos.tldr: The paper learns visual class prototypes from unlabeled test streams to mitigate a modality gap that prompt engineering alone cannot eliminate.

paragraphs: K-BTS brings feedback-driven iteration to structure-based molecular design. The paper contrasts the repeated Design-Make-Test-Analyze workflow used by experts with one-shot generative models that leave feedback disconnected from future design. It formulates iterative search as a dynamic hierarchical multi-armed bandit problem, allowing successive design decisions to use accumulated experience.

The framework separates decisions into two levels. An upper policy prioritizes promising molecular lineages, while a lower mechanism retrieves explicit chemical rules to steer language-model generation. Bayesian updates at both levels turn sparse docking scores into reusable information. This connects which molecular families receive attention with how candidates within them are generated.

On CrossDocked2020, K-BTS achieves the reported state-of-the-art Top-1 average docking score. The authors also report smooth, monotonic convergence that coordinates changes in molecular structure with improving affinity and characterize this behavior as search determinism. The findings support an iterative search process in which chemical knowledge and docking feedback jointly guide molecular refinement through successive rounds of generation.
icml-2026-steering-large-language-models.tldr: K-BTS uses hierarchical Bayesian search and chemical rules to steer iterative language-model molecular design using docking feedback.

paragraphs: TeamWork detects anomalies in time series containing multiple interacting variables. Such detection requires understanding both relationships between variables and patterns over time. The paper argues that existing methods often overlook differences in variables’ relative importance, making it difficult to model their contributions to normal system behavior effectively.

The framework assigns variables dominant or auxiliary roles according to how much they reduce uncertainty. Dominant variables drive system evolution, while auxiliary variables provide complementary information. A role-aware gated interaction module combines them while preserving this asymmetry. This gives the model a way to represent different contributions instead of treating all channels as equally influential.

TeamWork also uses period-aware masked modeling to learn temporal dependencies across short and long periods. Multiple specialized masking mechanisms address the fact that isolated-point and subsequence anomalies can appear differently across periodic systems. Experiments on several real-world datasets report stronger performance than state-of-the-art methods. The results support combining asymmetric channel relationships with temporal learning that explicitly spans different periods.
icml-2026-teamwork-multivariate-time-ser.tldr: TeamWork combines variable-specific roles with period-aware temporal modeling to improve multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

paragraphs: This paper studies policies that must remain robust when preferences change during an episode. After each transition, an opponent observes the new state and selects the next objective weights. Changing weights incurs a cost based on a Bregman divergence, controlled by a parameter that determines how strongly preference switching is penalized.

The authors formulate this interaction through a Bellman–Isaacs recursion, with an inner minimization over weights at every update. They prove that the resulting operator is a contraction and derive a certificate converting Bellman approximation error into a uniform robust-performance bound. Practical tabular and deep solvers combine Bregman-proximal weight updates with stabilized fixed-point iteration.

For evaluation, BR-K tests policies against multiple independently trained best-response preference adversaries, avoiding optimistic reuse of the critic. Across MO-Gymnasium benchmarks, the approach consistently improves the reported WRR measure against strong step-wise opponents relative to preference-conditioned baselines. The switching-cost parameter also provides smooth control over DRIFT. Together, the results connect a step-wise robustness model with solvable updates, performance certification, and adversarial evaluation.
icml-2026-time-consistent-robust-multi-o.tldr: The paper develops certified multi-objective policies robust to state-dependent preference changes, with switching costs controlling how freely an opponent can change weights.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether refusal is better understood as a process across layers and token positions than as a static direction in a final representation. Using causal tracing, the authors identify a sparse upstream activation pattern called a refusal trajectory. This pattern often remains present even when attacks such as GCG suppress terminal refusal signals.

Building on that observation, SALO detects jailbreaks using raw hidden-state volumes from a selected window of layers. It is a lightweight white-box detector, so its operation depends on access to internal model states. The central idea is to monitor earlier traces of refusal construction that may remain informative after the final refusal signal has weakened.

Across Qwen, Llama, and Mistral models, SALO improves detection for several attack families at a fixed operating point calibrated using XSTest. The paper also examines static representation baselines, sensitivity to the monitored region, adaptive GCG attacks, and encoded-input boundary cases. These analyses position refusal trajectories as a promising detection signal while explicitly investigating where their usefulness is limited.
icml-2026-tracing-the-dynamics-of-refusa.tldr: SALO detects jailbreaks by monitoring internal refusal trajectories that often persist after attacks suppress final refusal signals.

paragraphs: TVI-CoT addresses multimodal reasoning that proceeds entirely through text after an initial image encoding. In the setting described by the paper, later reasoning cannot revisit visual features and must depend on information captured initially. This restricts fine-grained inspection, checking earlier interpretations, and directing attention as the reasoning develops.

The framework introduces learnable Think, Look, and Answer control tokens. These let the model alternate between textual reasoning and access to visual features, selecting relevant image regions according to its evolving reasoning state. Visual grounding therefore becomes an explicit part of the reasoning sequence, allowing later reasoning steps to draw on image information when needed.

Experiments on eight benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance among multimodal language-model chain-of-thought methods. Reported gains over the baseline include 6.1% on MMMU, 3.8% on MathVerse, and 3.4% on both MathVista and ScienceQA. The findings support interleaving visual access with reasoning as a way to improve multimodal understanding, particularly where the reasoning process needs information beyond the initial visual description.
icml-2026-tvi-cot-text-visual-interleave.tldr: TVI-CoT lets multimodal models alternate between reasoning and targeted visual access, improving results across eight evaluated benchmarks.
